- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.36) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment <0.18) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays mean reversion, especially after sharp spikes — true prices revert faster than forecasted.
- Avoid overreacting to recent high sentiment — model tends to hold high forecasts even when sentiment cools.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — true prices often dip or stabilize sooner.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model averages too much — fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility spikes.
- Model underestimates price peaks when sentiment is high but recent price action is flat — misses momentum buildup.
